items.followUp: Define dipole-dipole forces and give one example.

rubric.why: A hydrogen bond forms when hydrogen is bonded to a highly electronegative atom and is attracted to another electronegative atom.
rubric.description: Defines the attraction involved in hydrogen bonding.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the attraction involving hydrogen and a highly electronegative atom.

rubric.why: A suitable example shows the student can identify a substance in which hydrogen bonding occurs.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct example, such as water, HF or ammonia.

modelAnswer: Hydrogen bonding is the attraction between a hydrogen atom bonded to a highly electronegative atom and a highly electronegative atom of another molecule.
For example, hydrogen bonding occurs between water molecules (H₂O).

items.followUp: What is meant by an ionic bond?

rubric.why: A chemical bond is an attractive force.
rubric.description: Identifies the bond as a force of attraction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a chemical bond is a force of attraction.

rubric.why: The force holds atoms or ions together in a substance.
rubric.description: States what the bond holds together.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the force holds atoms or ions together.

modelAnswer: A chemical bond is the force of attraction that holds atoms or ions together in a substance.

items.followUp: Give two examples of a solid dissolved in a liquid.

rubric.why: Carbon dioxide dissolved in water is a gas-in-liquid solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for an example such as carbon dioxide dissolved in water (soda water).

rubric.why: These are other examples of gases dissolved in liquids.
rubric.description: Gives a second correct gas-in-liquid solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second suitable example, such as oxygen dissolved in water.

modelAnswer: Carbon dioxide dissolved in water (soda water).

items.followUp: What is meant by a saturated solution?

rubric.why: An aqueous solution specifically uses water as its solvent.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that water is the solvent.

rubric.why: A solution contains solute dissolved in a solvent.
rubric.description: States that a substance is dissolved in the water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a solute or substance is dissolved in water.

modelAnswer: An aqueous solution is a solution in which water is the solvent and a solute is dissolved in it.

rubric.why: Molarity measures the amount of solute in moles.
rubric.description: Identifies the amount of solute as moles.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that molarity uses moles of solute.

rubric.why: The moles of solute are divided by the volume of the whole solution, usually in dm³ or litres.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for specifying volume of solution in litres or dm³.

modelAnswer: Molarity is the number of moles of solute dissolved per dm³ (litre) of solution.
M = moles of solute ÷ volume of solution in dm³.

items.followUp: Why is distilled water a poor conductor of electricity?

rubric.why: Acetic acid ionizes only partially in water, producing relatively few ions.
rubric.description: Explains why acetic acid is a weak electrolyte.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that acetic acid partially ionizes or produces few ions in water.

rubric.why: Calcium hydroxide is sparingly soluble in water, so its solution contains relatively few ions and conducts weakly.
rubric.description: Explains the weak conducting behaviour of calcium hydroxide solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for noting its low solubility or the small number of ions in solution.

modelAnswer: CH₃COOH is a weak electrolyte because it ionizes only partially in water and produces few ions.
Ca(OH)₂ is sparingly soluble in water, so its solution contains relatively few ions and conducts electricity weakly.

items.followUp: Why is the third ionization energy of magnesium much greater than the second?

rubric.why: After the first ionization, the remaining electron is being removed from a positively charged Mg⁺ ion.
rubric.description: Identifies the species from which the second electron is removed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the second electron is removed from Mg⁺ or a positive magnesium ion.

rubric.why: The positive ion attracts its remaining electrons more strongly, so more energy is needed to remove the second electron.
rubric.description: Explains why the second ionization energy is greater.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the stronger attraction to the greater energy required.

modelAnswer: After the first electron is removed, the second electron is removed from the positively charged Mg⁺ ion.
The remaining electrons are attracted more strongly by the positive ion, so more energy is required for the second ionization.

items.followUp: Name a metal that is a very good conductor of heat.

rubric.why: Mercury is commonly identified as a poor conductor of heat; some textbook treatments name lead as the poorest conductor among metals.
rubric.description: Names a metal identified as the least or a very poor conductor of heat.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for mercury; accept lead where that is the textbook convention used.

modelAnswer: Mercury (Hg) is a metal that is a poor conductor of heat.
